questions.q: What is a false positive in match review, as defined in this lesson?
options: Failing to merge two records that are actually the same entity
A correctly rejected candidate match
Merging two records that are actually different entities, contaminating one customer's data with another's
A system crash during the matching process
questions.explain: A false positive is an incorrect merge of two genuinely different entities, which the lesson describes as hard to detect and damaging to trust once discovered.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a false negative is a 'quieter' failure than a false positive?
options: Because it simply leaves a true duplicate unmerged, which defeats the point of MDM for that record but doesn't contaminate anything
Because false negatives never actually occur in practice
Because it actively corrupts other customers' data
Because false negatives are always caught immediately
questions.explain: The lesson contrasts the two: a false positive actively mixes two entities' data together, while a false negative just leaves a duplicate unresolved without corrupting anything.

questions.q: Which of these is listed as part of the match steward's job in this lesson?
options: Setting the company's annual marketing budget
Automatically deleting any record flagged for review without inspection
Confirming or rejecting a candidate pair based on the evidence, and fixing source data when that's the real problem
Writing the organization's Stripe payment integration
questions.explain: The lesson lists confirm/reject, fixing source data, and tuning rules as the steward's core responsibilities during match review.

questions.q: What are the three possible outcomes a steward can record for a reviewed match, per this lesson's workflow?
options: Merge, reject, or needs more data
Pass, fail, retry
Publish, archive, delete
Approve, deny, escalate to legal
questions.explain: The review workflow section lists merge, reject (confirmed different entities), and needs more data as the three recorded outcomes.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what does a pattern in how match reviews land over time provide?
options: Evidence that reference data governance is unnecessary
A reason to remove all human review from the process
A feedback signal that can inform tuning the match thresholds or weights from Lesson 7
Nothing useful — review outcomes are discarded after each case
questions.explain: The lesson states that stewardship isn't just case-by-case decisions — recorded review patterns feed back into improving the automated matching rules over time.
